summary: `src/store.js` now has `updateShelf(path, change)`, which takes a cross-process lock, re-reads the file, applies the change and saves unless the change refused. `saveShelf` now uses a unique temporary name per write, syncs before renaming, and cleans up on failure. Dead or older-than-30-second locks are broken safely; a live lock fails after 5s with `ShelfBusyError` (`code` `SHELF_BUSY`). `isHeld(book, at)` is the shared reservation reading, and `loadShelf` logs one warning per load, by book id only, for books held with no end date or an unreadable one. `docs/systems/store.md` records the protocol and why the lock exists. All 26 store tests pass, including 6 repeat runs in parallel, and the witness check passes (41/41, `T-27` id exact). Six deliberate breakages each failed the tests they target. After those runs I changed only a comment in `src/store.js` and the wording in `docs/systems/store.md`; the repeats and witness check ran after the comment change, and nothing was re-run after the doc edit. Changes are uncommitted for the executor.

notes: Contract for the reserve and keeper units: `change` edits the shelf in place and may be async. A refusal is the error `change` throws, passed through unchanged with nothing saved. `updateShelf` resolves to what `change` returned. Busy is `error.code === SHELF_BUSY` after 5s. Nothing but `updateShelf` should call `saveShelf`.

`src/pages.js:29` still tests `reservedBy === null` and does not use `isHeld`, so a lapsed reservation keeps showing 'reserved' until the page unit switches over. Left alone because of the non-goal (no pages).

With the seed data's b2, the server now writes one stderr warning per `GET /`, as A5 asks. `test/floor.test.js` pipes the server's stderr and never reads it; that is fine at today's request counts, but a later test making hundreds of requests should drain it.

The lock file holds only the pid, as D1 says. Holder identity comes from the inode, pinned by keeping the lock file open. Every removal of the lock goes through a short guard file, `<data file>.lock.guard.tmp`. See decisions.json for the alternatives rejected.

Two accepted gaps are documented in `docs/systems/store.md`. A crash while holding the guard, followed by a close interleave of waiters on a stale lock, could put two writers inside. A holder stalled past 30s exactly between its final check and its rename could overwrite the next writer.
An empty lock left by a crash between create and pid write is only broken by the 30s age rule, so callers get busy errors until then.

The read-only-directory test skips when run as root; it ran and passed here. The failed-rename test uses a directory as the data path, so no case has a rename failing over an existing data file; old-file safety on failure is shown by the read-only-directory and refusal tests.
No browser check was run: this unit adds no pages or routes.
